chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi', with an unbroken chain, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

By Allah, no one from us will come out before the emergence of the Qaim (peace be upon him) except that his example is like a nestling that flies from its nest before its wings have fully formed, so the young boys grab it and play with it.

key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.عَبَثُوا بِهِ: They played with it/toyed with it
key_terms.وَكْر: Nest, dwelling place of a bird

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor of the nestling in the hadith about the Qaim?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'waiting for the right moment' (Intizar) within Shia eschatology, warning against premature self-proclamation by the Ahl al-Bayt before the divinely appointed rise of Imam al-Qaim. The metaphor of the fledgling bird illustrates the vulnerability of those lacking established authority and divine backing, emphasizing that premature action leads to being easily subdued by rivals. This concept reinforces the scholarly view that the Mahdi's emergence is a specific, timed event rather than a result of individual initiative.

en.hubeali: H 14830 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e with an unbroken chain, has narrated the following: Aliasws Bin Al-Husaynasws has said:

‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! There will not come out any one from us<sup>asws</sup> before the coming out of Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> except that his example would be of a nestling trying to come out from its nest before its wings have been formed, so the young boys grab hold of it and play with it’.
en.sarwar: 383. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabi’e with an unbroken chain, has narrated the following: Ali (a.s.) Bin Al-Husayn (a.s.) has said:

‘By Allah (azwj)! There will not come out any one from us (a.s.) before the coming out of Al-Qaim (a.s.) except that his example would be of a nestling trying to come out from its nest before its wings have been formed, so the young boys grab hold of it and play with it’.
